decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark — Enter an address (+ optional title), it's validated and saved.” The client did not dispute URL-based saving, and Round 9 reports it delivered.
decisions.note: The presented save-by-URL behavior conforms to the reference. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Edit & delete — Fix or remove bookmarks, with a delete confirmation.”
decisions.note: This initial presentation includes individual deletion. A later revised presentation created a separate deletion-scope decision below. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Browse & open — See your list, click to open the original page.”
decisions.note: Opening the original URL conforms. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Find & organize — Search by keyword, tag bookmarks, filter by tag.”
decisions.note: A tag-filter capability is conforming as initially presented. Specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Manual entry — ... no automatic page-title/thumbnail fetching in v1.” Round 1 client: “I expect the app to collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image automatically.” Round 2 maker says automatic metadata capture is now in scope and was “previously excluded.”
decisions.note: The maker explicitly excluded required automatic metadata collection; the client supplied the conforming behavior. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker describes an “optional title” and generic editing but does not specify editing auto-collected title and description. Round 1 client requires automatic details “while letting me edit the title and description.” Round 2 maker explicitly adds that behavior.
decisions.note: The presented implementable scope lacked the required explicit metadata-editing behavior; the client extended it. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only says the spec “covers edge cases (duplicate links)” without stating the outcome. Round 1 client expresses the expectation: “Saving an address that already exists should take me to the existing bookmark for editing, not allow a duplicate.” Round 2 later presents the conforming rule.
decisions.note: The transcript does not establish whether the initially presented duplicate-link edge case was conforming or divergent. The client's expectation is recorded, but divergence cannot be inferred solely from that correction. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker summarizes browsing only as “See your list.” Round 1 client requires the normal list to “clearly show the title, description, tags, and favicon.” Round 2 maker lists those fields as newly covered.
decisions.note: The baseline scope lacked the required readability fields; the client supplied them. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only says “tag bookmarks.” Round 1 client explicitly requires “multiple tags,” and Round 2 maker presents “multiple tags” as now covered.
decisions.note: The client made multi-tag assignment explicit in the implementable specification. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope mentions tagging but no suggestions. Round 1 client requests “tag suggestions from tags I already use.” Round 2 maker adds “suggestions from tags you already use.”
decisions.note: Existing-tag autocomplete was missing and was added at the client's request. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposes only “Search by keyword.” Round 1 client specifies search across “title, description, note, and address.” Round 2 maker confirms those four fields.
decisions.note: The generic keyword-search decision did not specify the required full-text field coverage; the client corrected it. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents keyword search without case behavior. Round 1 client requires search “without caring about capitalization.” Round 2 maker adds “Case-insensitive” search.
decisions.note: Case-insensitive matching was absent from the presented search specification. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker mentions keyword search and tag filtering but no tag-search syntax. Round 1 client requests “`#tag` searches.” Round 2 maker adds `#tag`.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing tag-search syntax. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only keyword search. Round 1 client requests “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.” Round 2 maker adds those operators and grouping.
decisions.note: Boolean expressions and grouping were missing from the baseline search scope. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents keyword search without phrase syntax. Round 1 client requests “exact phrases.” Round 2 maker adds exact-phrase search.
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase search was missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 priority scope contains no read-later state. Round 1 client requires “an unread/read-later state.” Round 2 maker adds unread/read-later.
decisions.note: Read-later marking was absent and requested by the client. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope has no unread view. Round 1 client requests “separate unread ... views.” Round 2 maker adds a separate unread view.
decisions.note: The unread-only perspective was missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope has no read/unread state transition. Round 1 client requests an “unread/read-later state,” and Round 2 maker adds unread/read-later behavior; Round 9 reports read/unread controls.
decisions.note: The requested two-state behavior supplies the ability to mark an item read again, removing it from the unread perspective. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no bulk selection. Round 1 client requests “selecting several bookmarks for bulk changes.” Round 2 maker adds multi-select bulk changes.
decisions.note: Multi-bookmark bulk actions were missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no whole-result action. Round 1 client requests “applying an action to everything matching the current view.” Round 2 maker adds that capability.
decisions.note: Whole-current-view bulk actions were missing from the baseline scope. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope does not mention sorting. Round 1 client says “Please include sorting.” Round 2 maker adds sorting.
decisions.note: List sorting was missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no bookmark note. Round 1 client requires “a note.” Round 2 maker adds a note field.
decisions.note: Bookmark notes were missing; Markdown rendering was refined in a later decision. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no snapshot feature. Round 1 client requests “page snapshots—including keeping PDFs as PDFs.” Round 2 maker adds local page snapshots with PDF preservation.
decisions.note: Local snapshots and the PDF rule were missing. The HTML packaging detail was refined later. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no Internet Archive operation. Round 1 client requests “Internet Archive saving.” Round 2 maker adds submission to the Internet Archive.
decisions.note: Internet Archive saving was missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains deletion but no archive state. Round 1 client requires archiving and says archived links must be “hidden from normal browsing and search.” Round 2 maker adds that behavior.
decisions.note: Reversible hiding through archiving was absent. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope has no archive-only view. Round 1 client requests a “separate ... archived” view. Round 2 maker adds it.
decisions.note: The archived-only perspective was missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no saved filters. Round 1 client requests “saved reusable searches.” Round 2 maker adds named reusable searches.
decisions.note: Saved searches/bundles were missing. Included and excluded tags were refined later. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “no auto-import from a browser ... in v1.” Round 1 client: importing browser bookmarks “should not be ruled out” and requires Netscape-style import. Round 2 maker says browser import/export was “previously excluded” and is now in scope.
decisions.note: The client explicitly rejected the import exclusion. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope has no export. Round 1 client requests Netscape-style “import and export.” Round 2 maker adds both.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export was missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 scope contains no display preferences. Round 1 client requests “sorting, number of items shown, and font size.” Round 2 maker adds persisted display preferences.
decisions.note: Display-related personal settings were missing. Initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says only “edit title/description” without the required timing. Round 2 client specifies editing “both while saving where appropriate and afterward.” Round 3 maker adds this to scenarios and FR-004.
decisions.note: The revised specification still needed the before-and-after editing guarantee. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists title/description editing and separately lists notes and tags, but does not state that URL, tags, and note are editable. Round 2 client requires editing “address, title, description, tags, and note.” Round 3 maker adds the full field set.
decisions.note: The revised edit behavior covered too few bookmark fields. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2's detailed revised scope describes archive actions but omits individual permanent deletion. Round 2 client requires “permanently delete a single bookmark.” Round 3 maker adds FR-011 for permanent delete.
decisions.note: Although deletion appeared in the first baseline, it was absent from the detailed revised presentation and was restored by the client. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents archive behavior without explicitly distinguishing it from permanent removal. Round 2 client says “archiving should remain a separate, reversible action.” Round 3 maker adds separate reversible archive and permanent-delete requirements.
decisions.note: The archive/delete distinction and reversibility rule were not explicit until corrected. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2's revised feature table mentions tag suggestions and `#tag` search but does not retain an explicit tag-selection interaction. Round 2 client requires “Clicking a tag filters the list to that tag.” Round 3 maker adds US3 scenario 4 and FR-015.
decisions.note: The revised implementable specification omitted the concrete tag-selection filter behavior. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker includes a note but does not specify Markdown or rendering. Round 2 client requires “Notes support Markdown and are rendered when viewed.” Round 3 maker adds FR-007.
decisions.note: Plain/unspecified notes did not fulfill the Markdown-note requirement. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists full-text and `#tag` search independently without a combination rule. Round 2 client requires “A tag search combined with ordinary words requires both to match.” Round 3 maker adds implicit-AND behavior.
decisions.note: The combination semantics between tag and ordinary terms were missing. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds AND/OR/NOT and parentheses but omits how to search those words literally. Round 2 client requires quoted operators to be literal. Round 3 maker adds scenario 6 and FR-023.
decisions.note: The Boolean grammar lacked the required quoted-operator escape rule. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker defines saved searches only as “query+filters+sort.” Round 2 client requires they “specifically include some tags and exclude others.” Round 3 maker adds included/excluded tags to FR-030.
decisions.note: The bundle definition did not explicitly preserve included and excluded tag sets. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says “Local page snapshot (PDF kept as PDF)” but does not define webpage storage format. Round 2 client requires a “self-contained HTML file.” Round 3 maker adds that rule to FR-032.
decisions.note: The normal-webpage snapshot format remained underspecified until corrected. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker adds Netscape import/export without stating preserved fields. Round 2 client requires import to preserve “title, tags, and original date added.” Round 3 maker adds FR-035/036 and SC-007.
decisions.note: The import mapping lacked required preservation semantics. Second specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker's revision does not state tag-name uniqueness. Round 3 client requires that reusing a name refer to “that same tag throughout the collection.” Round 4 maker adds unique shared tag identity in three places.
decisions.note: The reference entity constraint that tag names identify a single shared tag was missing. Third specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker proposes asynchronous metadata (`pending`→`complete/failed`) without a rule protecting user edits. Round 5 client requires delayed details to “never overwrite a title or description I entered myself.” Round 6 maker adds user-set flags, conditional writes, and tests.
decisions.note: Without an explicit race safeguard, the asynchronous plan did not guarantee that before/after metadata edits would survive. Plan-review gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 presents US5 bulk tasks without full-filter semantics. Round 7 client says apply-to-all must respect search, clicked tag, unread/archive perspective, and saved-search include/exclude tags across later pages. Round 8 maker confirms it is “now” a full view descriptor “not just search words.”
decisions.note: The original task design scoped whole-result bulk actions too narrowly. The client corrected it to the complete current filtered collection. Tasks-review gate.
